definitions.explanation: the formal process of deciding on a matter through voting, especially in legislative contexts

examples.japanese: {法案|ほうあん}の{採決|さいけつ}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A vote was taken on the bill.

examples.japanese: {採決|さいけつ}の{結果|けっか}、{賛成|さんせい}{多数|たすう}で{可決|かけつ}された。
examples.english: As a result of the vote, it was passed by a majority in favor.

examples.japanese: {議長|ぎちょう}が{採決|さいけつ}を{取|と}ると{宣言|せんげん}した。
examples.english: The chairman announced that a vote would be taken.

notes:
FORMATION:
{採|さい} (pick, adopt) + {決|けつ} (decide) → deciding by picking/voting

VERB FORM:
{採決|さいけつ}する (to take a vote, to put to a vote)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {採決|さいけつ}を{取|と}る (to take a vote)
- {採決|さいけつ}に{付|ふ}す (to put to a vote)
- {強行|きょうこう}{採決|さいけつ} (railroading a vote through)

OUTCOMES:
- {可決|かけつ} (passage, approval)
- {否決|ひけつ} (rejection)

RELATED WORDS:
- {投票|とうひょう} (ballot, general voting)
- {決議|けつぎ} (resolution)
